newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro bourses up, jumpy ahead of US data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro bourses up, jumpy ahead of US data.

text.p: European stocks made modest gains on Friday but the mood was hesitant ahead of U.S. inflation figues due later which will give pointers on interest rates.
The dollar strengthened slightly against the yen although many currency dealers were reluctant to stick their necks out before the 1230 GMT release of U.S. producer price and retail sales data.
London made a healthy start after hefty losses on Thursday. The FTSE index climbed 0.3 percent with traders seeing only limited gains until the American data was out of the way.
"We're just seeing a bit of adjustment after yesterday, but a lot will depend on these (U.S. inflation) numbers this afternoon," said one trader.
Frankfurt and Paris also showed small gains after all European bourses registered losses on Thursday, unsettled by healthier U.S. employment figures which reignited inflation fears.
The poor performance followed a record-breaking pace by European bourses earlier this week which largely mirrored the bull market on Wall Street, hitherto driven by rapid growth and low inflation.
European investors closely follow the state of the U.S. economy, the world biggest, because any downturn would quickly be felt on this side of the Atlantic -- hence the focus on Friday's data.

Wall Street itself made losses on Thursday because of jitters over inflation. Economists in a Reuters survey said they expected September's retail sales to rise by 0.2 percent overall and the Producer Price Index to rise by 0.3 percent.
In Frankfurt, shares edged ahead slightly but were expected to tread water. "This is one of those 'let's wait for the Americans' kind of days," said a Frankfurt dealer.
Opinion was divided as to whether the DAX index, hovering at the 2,685 level, was taking a breather after its recent spate of record highs or heading for a more dramatic downward correction.
French shares made small gains but trading was thin. "The market is very cautious ahead of the U.S. data, you can see that in the volumes," a dealer said.
The dollar was unchanged against the mark but slightly stronger against the yen. Trade was light ahead of the U.S. data and was likely to remain so into the long U.S. Columbus Day weekend.

"After having taken its eye off U.S. inflation risks over the last week, the market could be in for a small shock if the prices data starts to turn higher now," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered Bank.

Among European currencies, sterling surged against the mark, touching fresh 20-month highs largely on the back of British finance minister Kenneth Clarke's upbeat speech at the ruling Conservative party conference on Thursday.

The pound broke through 2.40 marks in early business and pushed on by 1100 GMT to 2.4090, compared with 2.3943 late Thursday in Europe. It also rose strongly against the dollar to $1.5754, compared with $1.5656.
CURRENCIES AT 1100 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5298 marks and 111.47 yen compared with 1.5300 marks and 111.26 yen late in Europe on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1100 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 13.3 points at 4008.0.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 2.97 at 2,138.60.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 3.79 at 2684.54.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $381.85, compared with Thursday's close of $381.95. Silver was at $5.05, up four cents.
